children: Deutsche Bank is warning investors that a calm outlook for inflation, interest rates and economic growth may rest on unstable assumptions.

Global bond yields reached multiyear highs, yet equities and credit reflect resilient growth, easing inflation and modest central-bank tightening. Deutsche Bank's latest dislocations report argues that combination is becoming harder to defend as energy, food and commodity costs climb.

Brent crude traded around $96 a barrel, up from $82.49 one month earlier, as disruption around the Strait of Hormuz intensified. European natural-gas futures reached their highest level since early 2023, while sugar, wheat and corn prices surged during August.

Markets nevertheless expect energy costs to decline over the coming year. The six-month Brent contract near $83, versus $96.20 for front-month oil, effectively assumes shipping normalizes. If that assumption fails, inflation expectations, bond yields and valuations could reprice together.

The Federal Reserve presents another danger. Investors underestimated its hawkishness during four of the past five years, Deutsche Bank noted. Markets once expected two rate cuts by September, but received none and assign a 60% probability to a hike.

Meanwhile, August's ISM services prices-paid measure reached a four-year high, historically consistent with U.S. inflation above 5%. Similar complacency surrounds the European Central Bank despite stronger growth and higher energy prices.
Why Stock Investors Face a Narrower Escape Route
The threat is not simply higher inflation. An energy-driven supply shock can raise prices and weaken growth, squeezing corporate margins while preventing central banks from providing relief.

That leaves what Deutsche Bank called a very narrow landing zone. Stocks and credit can remain resilient if growth absorbs higher real yields and commodity pressures fade. But persistent inflation could force aggressive tightening precisely when expensive borrowing begins slowing demand.
For investors, oil, inflation surveys and Fed expectations now matter directly to equity valuations. That makes the next inflation report especially important.

title: Deutsche Bank Sees Stark Risk for Stock Market
